clue.text: Form congregation in a church service

parts.note: the Mass is the Catholic eucharistic church service

explanation.surface: A worshipper forms part of the congregation at a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather together into a crowd, just as a congregation is formed.

clue.text: Season's greetings, part one

parts.note: the first half of the setter's festive message, which continues in the other long down clue

explanation.walkthrough: Read with 8 down, the two long entries make the setter's festive wish to the paper's readers.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual festive wish opens the setter's greeting, a seasonal salutation.

clue.text: One bringing Christmas message and a sort of cake

definitions.meaning: the heavenly messenger who announced the birth of Jesus to the shepherds
a light sponge cake made with egg whites, named for this heavenly being

explanation.definitionFit: Gabriel's kind brought the Nativity news, and the airy sponge shares the heavenly name.

clue.text: Spirit of Christmas present moved him

definitions.text: Spirit of Christmas present moved him

parts.words: Spirit of Christmas present moved him
parts.note: in Dickens's A Christmas Carol the Ghost of Christmas Present helps change the old miser's heart

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit of Christmas present' reads like generosity, but it is the Dickens ghost who shows the miser of A Christmas Carol how others keep the feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's tight-fisted miser is reformed by the ghosts, among them the Spirit of Christmas Present.

clue.text: Person whose features are regular

parts.note: features read as newspaper articles: this writer turns in a regular piece, not someone with even facial features

explanation.walkthrough: 'Features' tempts you towards a face; here they are newspaper features appearing on a fixed schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper writer with a regular slot produces recurring feature pieces.

clue.text: Confine in small space in manger

definitions.meaning: to shut up in a cramped place, as in 'cabined, cribbed, confined'
a feeding trough, the infant Jesus's bed in the Nativity story

explanation.definitionFit: To be cribbed is to be cramped, and a crib is a feeding trough or Nativity cradle.

clue.text: Yule feature, rich sport in America

parts.note: the Yule log is a Christmas log or chocolate cake
rolling in it means very rich, so rolling means wealthy

explanation.surface: A Christmas log and a wealthy American's pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: In North America log rolling is a contest of balancing on a floating log while spinning it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumberjacks compete at spinning a floating timber underfoot, a competitive pastime in North America.

clue.text: Oratorio or mass he and I composed

indicators.note: composed says these letters are put together in a new arrangement, apt for music

explanation.surface: A choral work or a Mass written by him and me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges MASS, HE and I; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel's Messiah is a celebrated oratorio, often performed at Christmas.

clue.text: Simplicity of full Christmas accommodation in the old days around church

parts.note: the inn at Bethlehem had no room, so it was full

indicators.note: around says the word for formerly wraps round the church letters

parts.note: once means formerly, in times past
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The plain fact that there was no room at the inn long ago, beside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The inn of the Nativity story had no room for Mary and Joseph.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocence is guilelessness, an artless naivety or simplicity.

clue.text: Season's greetings, part two

parts.note: the second half of the setter's festive message, addressed to the people tackling the puzzle

explanation.walkthrough: Read after 1 down, it completes the setter's Christmas Eve wish to the paper's readers.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter addresses the festive wish to puzzle-doers, completing the seasonal salutation.

clue.text: English going mad around end of year and overindulging

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters wrap round the next piece
going mad says the letters of the word going are scrambled
end of picks the final letter of the word year

explanation.surface: An Englishman goes wild at the close of the year, eating and drinking too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' turns GOING into OGING, and 'around' puts R (from 'end of year') inside it after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorging oneself to bursting point is excessive feasting, a synonym for overindulging.

clue.text: Christmas visitor contributing to pleasant anticipation

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A festive caller adds to the happy excitement of waiting for the big day.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas is the night-time caller who delivers presents on Christmas Eve.

clue.text: Give a decision about game before Christmas comes round

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a common crossword game

indicators.note: comes round says the word for Christmas is turned to read backwards

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone must settle a dispute over a game before the festive season arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who rules on a matter delivers a verdict concerning it.

clue.text: Goat at Christmas, for example, is this

definitions.text: Goat at Christmas, for example, is this

parts.words: Goat at Christmas, for example, is this
parts.note: the Goat is Capricorn, the star sign whose dates cover late December, so it describes a sign of the astrological belt

explanation.walkthrough: Capricorn, symbolised by a goat, runs from about 22 December to 19 January, so the Goat is the sign in force at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn the Goat is one of the twelve signs of that astrological belt, so it is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Butcher trims ducks and pieces of turkey

indicators.note: to butcher is to hack about, so the following letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A butcher prepares ducks and joints of turkey for Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' looks like a noun, the trader, but is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower legs of a cooked bird are its drumsticks, joints carved from the turkey.

clue.text: Dealt with arch needing repair in church

indicators.note: needing repair says these letters are broken and must be put back together differently

explanation.surface: A builder has dealt with an arch that needed fixing in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing repair' rearranges DEALT and ARCH together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is a large principal church, the seat of a bishop.

clue.text: Note real change around Christmas, primarily goodwill towards men?

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround the chosen letter
change says the letters of note and real are altered into a fresh order
primarily picks the first letter of the word Christmas

explanation.surface: Notice a real shift in the festive season, mainly peace and goodwill to all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' gives TOLERANE and 'around' wraps it round C; the question mark admits that tolerance is only one example of goodwill to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbearance and acceptance of others is one form of goodwill to fellow people; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Oriental with faith in British industry

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the run of the words British industry

explanation.surface: An Asian worker of religious conviction is employed in a British factory.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'British' into 'industry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Hinduism, a religion of the Indian subcontinent, is an Eastern believer.

clue.text: Holy object Catholic priest protected

indicators.note: protected means the Catholic letters stand guard around the priest

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest kept a sacred artefact safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a venerated remnant of a saint, kept as a sacred item.

clue.text: Assemble close to archdeacon in church

indicators.note: in says the preceding pieces are placed inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
on can mean near or next to, as in on the coast
VEN is short for Venerable, the formal title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: Gather near the archdeacon inside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon in the Church of England is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To convene is to call or come together, a synonym for assembling.

clue.text: Agents of grace Hamlet associated with angels

definitions.text: Agents of grace Hamlet associated with angels

parts.words: Agents of grace Hamlet associated with angels
parts.note: refers to Hamlet's cry on seeing the ghost, 'Angels and ... of grace defend us!', where these agents stand beside angels

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Hamlet, Act 1 Scene 4, the prince cries 'Angels and ministers of grace defend us!' when the ghost appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Servants who carry out divine grace are its agents, the word Hamlet pairs with angels.

clue.text: Cuts man off in holy place

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone excludes a man from a sacred spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CUTS and MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is the inner sacred part of a temple, a holy precinct.

clue.text: Peace has withered-it must be sought in New Year

parts.note: sere is a poetic word for dried up or withered

indicators.note: must be sought in says the word it is placed inside the letters for New Year

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New Year

explanation.surface: Calm has faded, and it will have to be looked for again in January.
explanation.definitionFit: Serenity is calm tranquillity, a state of inner peace.

clue.text: Gift for Christmas, perhaps — it comes but once a year

definitions.meaning: a children's yearly book of stories and puzzles, a typical Christmas present

definitions.text: it comes but once a year
definitions.meaning: something that happens yearly, echoing the saying about Christmas

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an annual is a hardback children's book tied to a comic or TV show, sold as a Christmas present each year.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearly hardback book is a stock stocking-filler, and anything yearly recurs every twelve months.

clue.text: Practising top-class carol

parts.note: U stands for upper class
to carol is to sing joyfully

explanation.surface: A superior choir rehearsing a Christmas song.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class is an old British label for refined speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: To be using something is to employ it, as when practising a craft.

clue.text: Popular Christmas Oratorio initially included as sacred work

indicators.note: included says those first letters go inside the word for popular

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: initially picks the first letters of the words Christmas and Oratorio

explanation.surface: A well-liked Christmas Oratorio was at first counted as a holy composition.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a sacred painting of Christ or a saint in Orthodox devotion.

clue.text: Moderate sort of pie

definitions.meaning: to soften or tone down, as in not choosing one's words harshly
a small sweet pastry filled with dried fruit eaten at Christmas

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' is a verb here, as in 'not mincing words'; a mince pie is the British Christmas pastry of spiced dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincing one's words tones them down, and mince pies are the festive fruit pastries.

clue.text: Mark on skin made by cold ice, mostly — it takes only a moment

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: mostly says the word ice loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
a thing done in a trice takes only a moment, so a trice is a moment

explanation.surface: Cold ice can leave a scar on the skin in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ICE to IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicatrice is the scar left by a healed wound, a lasting blemish on the body.

clue.text: Author is one remembered on Boxing Day, we hear, by child

indicators.note: we hear says the saint's name is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: St Stephen's Day is 26 December, Boxing Day in Britain
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A writer is a saint commemorated after Christmas, next to a little one.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing Day, 26 December, is St Stephen's feast day; STEPHEN said aloud gives STEVEN. Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was a Scottish novelist, a famous writer.

clue.text: He provided one of the most original Christmas presents

definitions.text: He provided one of the most original Christmas presents

parts.words: He provided one of the most original Christmas presents
parts.note: original means first: one of the wise men brought gold, frankincense or myrrh to the infant Jesus, the very first Christmas gifts

explanation.walkthrough: 'most original' means not inventive but the very first: the gifts of the Magi.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the three wise men from the East is called a magus, a gift-bearer at the Nativity.
